name: Senegal
summary_text: Senegal criminalises same-sex sexual activity under Article 319 of the 1965 Penal Code, which carries a maximum of five years' imprisonment. The provision is enforced: in September 2018 four LGBT people, two women and two men, were detained in Dakar on charges of "acts against the order of nature" after videos of them circulated, part of a wave of politically motivated detentions in the run-up to the 2019 elections.  A campaign to raise the maximum penalty to 15 years has run since 2020, with anti-LGBT forces pressing for the increase as of July 2024. The maximum sentence remains five years; the proposal has not been reported as enacted.  Official hostility extends to speech on the subject. A political activist and a preacher were jailed and fined 100,000 CFA francs each after posting a video attacking opposition leader Ousmane Sonko for allowing a visiting French politician to express support for same-sex marriage. The US State Department's 2012 human rights report on Senegal listed pre-electoral violence, torture, and violence and discrimination against lesbian, gay, bisexual and transgender persons among the country's major human-rights problems.  Violence by non-state actors is documented at extreme scale. In November 2023 the body of a 31-year-old man, named locally as Cheikh Fall, was dug up from a cemetery and burned in the street after it became known that he was gay. Four men were arrested in connection with the incident; images from the scene show a crowd of hundreds gathered around the fire.

sources.title: 2026 law lengthening penalties for 'unnatural acts' - Sonko bill adopted March 12, signed by President Bassirou Diomaye Faye March 30
sources.documents: New legal status: 5 to 10 years prison for 'unnatural acts', fines 100,000 to 10 million CFA francs vs 1.5 million prior, ban on 'promotion, financing and support of homosexuality, bisexuality and transsexuality', penalty for 'abusive relationships conducted in bad faith'; June 2026 constitutional amendment banning same-sex marriage.
sources.detail: Presented 25 February 2026 by Prime Minister Ousmane Sonko as campaign promise; adopted March 12; signed March 30 2026 and published in official gazette following day; June 2026 National Assembly voted unanimously to amend Constitution. No URL visible.

sources.documents: Government report on criminal prosecution, widespread discrimination, social intolerance, acts of violence; media failure to report anti-LGBT hatred/violence; drop in reported cases due to going underground, international attention, legal challenges.
sources.detail: Long block quote reproduced in article; also cites July 2011 State Dept information on adoption eligibility. No URL visible.

sources.title: U.S. Department of State 2012 Human Rights Report on Senegal
sources.documents: Government report on 2012 enforcement: arrest, discrimination, police harassment including arrest on second-hand reports and poor treatment in detention; January arrest of two women over kissing video; October Dakar court sentence.
sources.detail: Quotes: Tasmir Jupiter Ndiaye sentenced to 4 years + 200,000 CFA francs ($400) for 'acts against nature' plus arms/battery; Matar Diop 3 years. Women held then released on bail, never formally charged. No URL visible.

sources.documents: Rights machinery: recommendations to amend Penal Code to decriminalize, end prohibition, release prisoners, moratorium on Article 319, anti-discrimination and dialogue; Senegal's refusal/defense citing culture, religion, social cohesion.
sources.detail: Lists recommending states (UK, Belgium, Canada, Netherlands, Slovenia, Czech Republic, Ireland, Uruguay, Argentina, Austria, Germany, Mexico, Brazil, Greece, Paraguay, Thailand, Switzerland); Senegal responses summarized plus statements by Foreign Minister Madické Niang 6 February 2009 and Justice Minister Sidiki Kaba 21 October 2013: 'There is no criminalization of homosexuality... Article 319 talks about acts contrary to nature.' No URL visible.

sources.title: United Nations Working Group on Arbitrary Detention - March 2010 finding
sources.documents: Finding that Senegal National Police detained persons alleged to have committed 'unnatural sexual acts'; recommendation on detentions for decency/public morality.
sources.detail: Quoted recommendation: 'Pay particular attention to detentions on the grounds of offending decency or public morality, with a view to avoiding any possible discrimination against persons of a different sexual orientation'. No URL visible.
